$comment: Style pack: Character Lighting. Learned from the user's reference Short Video-9968 (a 3D head shown under six lighting setups, each cut on the narrator's cue word, with a top-down light plot below and yellow captions on the seam; measured for technique only, no footage, character, voice or copy taken) and the user's setup breakdown (front = innocence, split = secrecy, under = threat, top = unreadable eyes, blue backlight = coldness, three-point = heroism). The relight is 2D light shaping on real footage: shadows and pools that follow the tracked face (rcg track), the background dropped and rim light drawn from the subject matte (rcg matte). Workflow and judgment: .agents/skills/style-character-lighting/SKILL.md.
label: Character Lighting
use: Light a character to say who they are: relight real footage per beat (front, split, under, top, blue backlight, three-point, Rembrandt, loop, butterfly, noir, dual colour, silhouette), explain lighting with a top-down light plot, tag the mood a setup carries. Lighting explainers, character reveals, story beats that turn (innocent to guilty, calm to threat), cinematic talking heads.
from: the user's reference Video-9968 + the user's character lighting breakdown (learned, nothing copied)

label.$note: bundled; tracked uppercase setup names and plot labels

strong.$note: bundled; the meaning word on a mood tag

captions.$note: The reference's caption: a short phrase in bold yellow sans on a dark rounded pill. In the stage layout it sits on the seam between the footage and the light plot (--y 950); on full-frame footage use the normal caption lane.

motion.$note: Light changes are hard cuts on the cue word by default (the reference). fade and flicker are for a light switching on inside a shot. Plot lights slide from the previous setup when from= is set.

sfx.$note: A light switching is a click, not a whoosh. Most relights need no sound; use one on a reveal.
